## What we learned

Engineering notation writes a value as a number from **1 to less than 1000** multiplied by a power of 10 whose exponent is a **multiple of 3**.

Examples:

- **27 000 = 27 × 10³**
- **0.00047 = 470 × 10⁻⁶**

If the exponent changes, move the decimal point in the coefficient so the value stays the same.

Engineering notation is especially useful in electronics because its powers of 10 line up with metric prefixes. [[1, pp. 6–8]](../../references.qmd#ref-grob2016)
